title: Music in Ancient China and India
objective: After this level you can describe early musical traditions in China and India.
summary: China's Zeng bells (about 2,400 years old) sound two notes each and carry music-theory inscriptions; the ba yin sorted instruments by material. India's Samaveda set verses to melody.

cards.headline: In 1978, a tomb in China held the world's largest set of bronze bells.
cards.body: They belonged to Marquis Yi of Zeng, and they're about 2,400 years old. Strike one bell in two places and it sings two different notes. Far to the southwest, India had its own way of turning sacred words into song. Two ancient traditions, one level.

cards.headline: One bell, two notes
cards.body: The Zeng bells, from Suizhou in Hubei province, are the largest and best-preserved set of bronze bells in the world. They follow a 'one bell, two tones' system: each sounds two notes, depending on where it's struck. And they carry 3,755 characters of inscriptions about music theory, the earliest surviving archaeological documents to show mathematical relationships in music. Remember Level 22's ratios? China was doing the math too, in bronze.

cards.headline: Eight sounds, sorted by material
cards.body: Ancient China sorted its orchestras in its own way. The ba yin, or eight sounds, dating from the Western Zhou dynasty, grouped instruments by what they were made of: stone, earth (pottery), bamboo, metal, skin, silk, wood and gourd. The Zeng bells go straight into the metal group. It's a system you could almost run from a well-stocked craft cupboard.

cards.headline: India: the Veda of chants
cards.body: In India, the Samaveda, the 'Knowledge of the Chants', gathered verses mostly from the older Rigveda and arranged them to be sung to fixed melodies during rituals. A specialist priest, the udgatri, sang them, stretching, repeating and pausing on syllables so the words fit the tune. The words came first; the melody reshaped them.

cards.fact: India wrote a handbook for the whole stage.
cards.context: The Natyashastra, attributed to the sage Bharata and dated between the 1st century BCE and the 3rd century CE, is a detailed treatise on Sanskrit theater. It covers dance, music, poetics and aesthetics together. India's ragas and talas get their own level in Chapter 6.

cards.headline: China and India: visited
learned: The Zeng bells: about 2,400 years old, two notes each
Their inscriptions link music and mathematics
Ba yin: instruments sorted into eight materials
Samaveda chants and the Natyashastra's theater

questions.prompt: Match each name with what it means or describes.
questions.explanation: The Zeng bells follow a 'one bell, two tones' system, ba yin means the eight sounds, the Samaveda is the 'Knowledge of the Chants', and the Natyashastra is a treatise on Sanskrit theater.

questions.prompt: How did the Samaveda turn verses into ritual music?

options.label: By arranging them to be sung to fixed melodies
By adding drum parts for dancers
options.rationale: The Samaveda is about singing the verses, not drums.

options.label: By writing brand-new poems for each separate ritual
options.rationale: Most of its verses come from the older Rigveda.

options.label: By translating them into Greek
options.rationale: It stayed within India's own Vedic tradition.

questions.explanation: The Samaveda arranged verses, mostly from the Rigveda, to be sung to fixed melodies by the udgatri priest.

questions.prompt: What do the Zeng bell inscriptions share with the ancient Greek ratios for musical intervals?

options.label: Both come from the same teacher
options.rationale: They arose separately, in China and in Greece.

options.label: Both link musical notes to mathematics
Both sort instruments by their material
options.rationale: That's China's ba yin, not the Greek ratios.

options.label: Both name notes after a hymn
options.rationale: Naming notes after a hymn comes later, with Guido.

questions.explanation: The Zeng inscriptions are the earliest surviving documents of mathematical relationships in music; the Greeks tied intervals to ratios.
